reviewType: targeted primary-source review; not exhaustive or systematic

sources.title: Fast and Exact Rule Mining with AMIE 3
sources.inspection: Lajus, Galárraga, Suchanek (2020), [Fast and Exact Rule Mining with AMIE 3](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7250613/), full article, especially support/confidence, PCA and pruning
sources.contribution: Mines relational rules with exact scoring options and bounded language/search settings; discusses alternatives for incomplete evidence.
sources.limits: Exactness concerns its configured rule space and metrics, not truth or useful software composition. Partial Completeness Assumption is a modeling assumption; absence is not inherently a negative.
sources.application: Define explicit rules and denominators; compare observed-world and completeness-qualified metrics. Do not adopt PCA silently.

sources.title: gSpan: Graph-Based Substructure Pattern Mining
sources.inspection: Yan and Han (2002), [gSpan: Graph-Based Substructure Pattern Mining](https://sites.cs.ucsb.edu/~xyan/papers/gSpan-short.pdf), author-hosted paper
sources.contribution: Canonical minimum DFS codes support search for frequent connected labeled subgraphs; support counts graphs containing a pattern.
sources.limits: A frequent pattern is not an implication, abstraction boundary or behavior contract. Selected implementation must demonstrably preserve direction, labels and port distinctions.
sources.application: Motif baseline and candidate generation. Keep graph-level support distinct from occurrence counts and family-level support.

sources.title: Workflow Patterns
sources.inspection: van der Aalst, ter Hofstede, Kiepuszewski, Barros, [Workflow Patterns](https://www.vdaalst.com/publications/p108.pdf), author-hosted paper, introduction and pattern descriptions
sources.contribution: Names recurring control-flow requirements such as sequence, split and synchronization, independent of a single product.
sources.limits: The catalog is a semantic vocabulary, not automatic rule mining. A data edge alone does not establish control-flow or concurrency semantics.
sources.application: Label relation kinds explicitly; use patterns as interpretation prompts and competing explanations rather than training truth.

sources.title: Process Discovery and Exploration
sources.inspection: Leemans (2015), [Process Discovery and Exploration](https://leemans.ch/publications/papers/dc2014leemans.pdf), full short paper
sources.contribution: Frames process discovery from execution event logs, distinguishes fitness, precision and generalization, and discusses rediscoverability assumptions.
sources.limits: Our static template graphs are not execution traces. Historical state-of-the-art statements in this paper are not current claims.
sources.application: Borrow the separation of fit, overgeneralization and future-case behavior; do not claim an event-log discovery method applies unchanged to templates.

sources.title: Components overview
sources.inspection: Langflow, [Components overview](https://docs.langflow.org/components/), official documentation: ports, dynamic ports, output selection and versions
sources.contribution: Components expose typed ports; configuration can affect ports and selected outputs. Saved occurrences can retain an older component state.
sources.limits: Current online documentation may differ from archived exports. Type compatibility and current names do not prove historical compatibility or task success.
sources.application: Extract from each saved occurrence and pin its evidence. Preserve native type/version, port handle, output selection, required fields and uncertainty.

sources.title: The Algebra of Open and Interconnected Systems
sources.inspection: Fong (2016), [The Algebra of Open and Interconnected Systems](https://arxiv.org/abs/1609.05382), author abstract
sources.contribution: Develops compositional mathematics for networks of components with typed terminals using hypergraph categories and related constructions.
sources.limits: This review inspected the abstract, not its proofs. No categorical laws or semantic preservation are established for our JSON representation without an explicit interpretation.
sources.application: Model an assembly as an open graph with an external interface; preserve boundary mappings when packaging. Formal inspiration, not an imported proof.

sources.title: Abstraction, Composition and Contracts: A Sheaf Theoretic Approach
sources.inspection: Speranzon, Spivak, Varadarajan (2018), [Abstraction, Composition and Contracts: A Sheaf Theoretic Approach](https://arxiv.org/abs/1802.03080), author abstract
sources.contribution: Distinguishes wiring, behavior and abstraction for interconnected systems through a common formal framework.
sources.limits: Abstract-level inspection; adapting its semantics requires actual behavioral models. Static templates supply insufficient evidence for that alone.
sources.application: Keep structural fit, declared behavior and validated behavior as separate fields. Boundary proposals cannot silently inherit behavioral guarantees.

sources.title: Shapes Constraint Language
sources.inspection: W3C (2017), [Shapes Constraint Language](https://www.w3.org/TR/shacl/), official Recommendation: abstract, shapes and validation model
sources.contribution: Separates data graphs from graph-expressed constraints used for conformance checking.
sources.limits: SHACL is for RDF and checks declared constraints. It is not itself a workflow miner, synthesizer or proof of operational correctness.
sources.application: Adopt the separation of data, constraints and validation report. RDF/SHACL is an optional adapter, not a prerequisite for JSON interchange.

sources.title: PROV-O
sources.inspection: W3C (2013), [PROV-O](https://www.w3.org/TR/prov-o/), official Recommendation: entities, activities, derivation and revision
sources.contribution: Represents derivation chains and responsibility across data artifacts and processing activities.
sources.limits: A recorded origin is an audit trail, not a guarantee of authenticity, licensing sufficiency or validity.
sources.application: Trace source export → normalized graph → fact → rule witness → candidate composite; preserve duplicate origins and extraction version.

sources.title: Genetic Programming
sources.inspection: DEAP, [Genetic Programming](https://deap.readthedocs.io/en/master/tutorials/advanced/gp.html), official implementation tutorial, especially strongly typed GP
sources.contribution: Provides explicit primitive/terminal types and type-matched tree construction, with implementation caveats on available terminals.
sources.limits: This is implementation documentation, not the original Montana paper or evidence about our task. Tree representations do not naturally preserve shared DAG substructure.
sources.application: Candidate approach for evolving rule expressions or typed constructor programs. Grammar completeness, depth bounds, deterministic validation and scoring remain ours to design.

sources.title: Cartesian Genetic Programming
sources.inspection: Miller and Thomson (2000), [Cartesian Genetic Programming](https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-540-46239-2_9), original publisher abstract
sources.contribution: Encodes programs as indexed graphs using connection/function genes and studies evolutionary search and neutrality on example tasks.
sources.limits: Publisher abstract inspected; attempted repository PDF was inaccessible. Original benchmark success does not establish compatibility with Langflow resource semantics, ports or composite boundaries.
sources.application: More direct graph-search inspiration than evolving neural weights. Require typed gene references, bounded topology operators and a separate legality/evidence evaluator.

sources.title: Evolving Neural Networks through Augmenting Topologies
sources.inspection: Stanley and Miikkulainen (2002), [Evolving Neural Networks through Augmenting Topologies](https://nn.cs.utexas.edu/downloads/papers/stanley.ec02.pdf), original author-hosted paper, topology mutation, historical markings and ablations
sources.contribution: Evolves neural topology and weights; aligns inherited structures, protects variation through speciation and grows structure.
sources.limits: Neural activation/weight semantics differ from workflow components. A new encoding, constraints and task-specific fitness are necessary; fast learning of our rules is unestablished.
sources.application: Consider lineage, diversity and incremental growth as design ideas. Do not rename a workflow graph search NEAT unless its adaptation is specified and compared.

sources.title: Cross-validation: grouped data
sources.contribution: Group-aware splits prevent the same specified group from appearing in both training and testing; group sizes can be imbalanced.
sources.limits: Quality depends on correct groups. Splitting by repository alone does not stop copied templates crossing splits.
sources.application: Group graph variants by source lineage/content families before splitting; record uncertainty and family-balanced as well as graph-weighted summaries.

sources.title: On Over-fitting in Model Selection and Subsequent Selection Bias in Performance Evaluation
sources.inspection: Cawley and Talbot (2010), [On Over-fitting in Model Selection and Subsequent Selection Bias in Performance Evaluation](https://www.jmlr.org/papers/v11/cawley10a.html), original journal abstract
sources.contribution: Shows that optimizing a finite-sample model-selection criterion can itself overfit and bias evaluation.
sources.limits: Abstract-level inspection. It supplies no numeric sample requirement or guaranteed correction for this corpus.
sources.application: Separate development tuning from evaluation; record every inspection and reserve fresh families for changed hypotheses. Miners, thresholds and evolutionary fitness all create selection opportunities.
